svg.title: URL and network bounds — okfy security explainer
svg.desc: The rules that keep every request same-origin and inside the declared bundle root. A URL is accepted only when its scheme is http or https, its origin equals the page's own origin, its path starts with the root path which ends in a slash, and it carries no username, password, query, fragment or encoded separator. A URL from another origin, a path above the root, a URL with credentials, a query or a fragment, an encoded separator, or a path that traverses above the root is refused. Every request is made with credentials omitted and redirects treated as errors, so a response can neither carry a cookie nor bounce the request to another host; each request holds one of four fetch slots with a thirty-second deadline and a bounded body read, the pending queue is capped at sixty-four, a body that is never used is cancelled rather than buffered, and the response's own URL is checked again against the root so a server cannot answer from outside it. A link resolves to candidate paths anchored at the file's own directory and each ancestor; a candidate already in the loaded set resolves without a request, only a 404 tries the next candidate and any other failure is final, the crawl schedules each URL once, and the on-demand path remembers which URLs it has already tried. Inside the fence the tool can reach the entry file and every file a link resolves to, a sibling caption track, an image only as a blob URL of its own bytes, a served clip read once and then played from its blob, a local clip that streams from an object URL and never touches the network, and the page's own manifest icons. Refused at the fence are another origin, a path above the bundle root, a redirect, an external or data image from content, and any URL carrying credentials, a query or a fragment. The assistant is the single path that leaves the origin, a POST to the provider the user configures over https or over http on loopback with a bind-all address normalized to the loopback address; it does not go through the bundle fetch path, so every rule above still governs every bundle request, and the policy's connect-src is the gate. The rules constrain URLs, not the server's mapping from URLs to files, so symlinks, internal rewrites and a misconfigured deploy remain the server's business.
svg.text: Every request same-origin and under the bundle root, with no credentials and no redirects
A URL is checked before any request is made — and again on the response
the page's origin, under the root, nothing else
The check runs on the URL the tool resolved and once more on the URL the response reports.
a body read with a bound
Sixty-four requests may wait at once, and a body the tool does not use is cancelled rather than buffered.
A 404 is the only failure that moves on: a blocked, refused or redirecting URL is left alone.
Credentials are omitted, so a bundle request carries nothing the origin could act on.
Refusing redirects is what makes the root check final: a bounce cannot carry the request somewhere else.
A link becomes candidates, and a candidate becomes a request
anchored at the file's own directory and at each ancestor, up to the root
a candidate already loaded resolves with no request at all
only a 404 tries the next candidate; another failure is final
the crawl schedules each URL once, and the on-demand path remembers what it tried
Alternative paths are the one concession: a link written for a nested collection still resolves, and a miss
is answered by another candidate rather than by a retry.
4 · Inside the fence, and outside it
What the same origin and the root let through, and what they stop
the entry file, and each file a link resolves to
a sibling caption track for a clip
an image, only as a blob URL of its bytes
a served clip, read once, played from its blob
a local clip: an object URL, no network at all
another origin — a different host or scheme
a path above the bundle root
a redirect: the bounce is a failure, not a hop
an external or data: image from content
credentials, a query or a fragment
So a malicious bundle cannot probe another host, read another origin, or smuggle a resource in through a redirect.
The assistant, and the limits of the rules
a POST to the provider you configure, over https — or http on loopback
so every rule on this page still governs every bundle request
connect-src allows the page's own origin and the provider's endpoints
the rules bind URLs, not how a server turns them into files: symlinks and rewrites are its job
publish on a dedicated static origin, without sensitive routes
The rules constrain URLs, not the server's mapping from URLs to files. Symlinks, internal rewrites and a
misconfigured deploy are handled on the server; the tool's part is to refuse every URL outside its own root.
